name: lentil cottage pie
instructions:
Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie — a vegetarian cottage pie with a root-vegetable base (leeks, carrots, swede/rutabaga, celeriac/celery root), tinned green lentils, dried porcini + marmite as the umami backbone, cumin seeds as an unusual aromatic, and crispy fried rosemary on top. Topped with mashed potatoes (cottage pie format) and baked until golden. Written down here as a scaffold — a proven working recipe in the tradition we want to advance from (see EXPERIMENTAL DIRECTIONS in notes for the modifications we're planning to try on top of this baseline).

SERVES 6-8. Total time ~2 hours. Oven 190°C / 375°F.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

Root-vegetable filling:
- 10g dried porcini mushrooms (or ~1 tbsp porcini mushroom powder + 600ml boiling water)
- 600 ml boiling water (for the porcini)
- 2 large leeks
- 3 carrots
- 500g swede (rutabaga)
- 500g celeriac (celery root)
- 2 tbsp olive oil (plus more as needed)
- 3 sprigs fresh rosemary
- 1 tsp cumin seeds
- 1 yellow onion (quartered — gets blended)
- 1 tsp marmite
- 3 tbsp tomato paste (tomato purée in UK terms)
- 1 × 400g tin green lentils (with the juices)
- sea salt and black pepper to taste

Mash topping:
- 2 kg potatoes
- 40 g unsalted butter
- splash of milk
- salt and pepper to taste

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. PREHEAT the oven to 190°C / 375°F. Blend the porcini mushrooms with 600ml boiling water — set aside to steep and reconstitute.

2. PREP THE VEGETABLES: trim and slice the leeks into ~2cm thick rounds. Scrub and chop the carrots, swede, and celeriac to similar sizes (~2 cm chunks).

3. CRISPY ROSEMARY: heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large casserole pan over medium heat. Strip the rosemary leaves from the stems into the hot oil. Fry ~1 minute until crispy. Remove the rosemary to a plate — save for garnish. This flavors the oil.

4. TOAST + COOK THE VEGETABLES: add the cumin seeds and the prepared root vegetables to the rosemary-flavored oil. Season with salt and pepper. Cook 30 min, stirring regularly, until softened and starting to caramelize.

5. Meanwhile, MAKE THE MASH: peel and chop the potatoes. Boil in salted water ~15 min until tender. Drain well. Mash with the 40 g butter and a splash of milk. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

6. BLEND THE UMAMI PASTE: put the quartered onion into the food processor with the porcini mushrooms (and their soaking liquid), the marmite, and the tomato paste. Blend until smooth.

7. ADD THE UMAMI PASTE TO THE VEGETABLES: pour the blended mixture into the vegetable pan. Cook ~20 min, stirring frequently, until dark and caramelized.

8. ADD THE LENTILS: stir in the tinned green lentils along with their juices. Bring to a boil. Season to taste.

9. ASSEMBLE + BAKE: transfer the filling to a baking dish (or leave it in an oven-safe casserole). Spoon the mash over the top and spread evenly. Place on a tray and bake ~30 min until lightly golden on top and bubbling at the edges.

10. SERVE: sprinkle the reserved crispy rosemary on top just before serving. Traditional accompaniment: steamed seasonal greens (peas, spinach, kale).
notes:
Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie — from The Happy Foodie / Jamie Oliver's Veg. Written down here as a SCAFFOLD/BASELINE. The recipe as-written is a proven working british vegetarian cottage pie; the accumulated notes below capture what I've learned from earlier iterations (as [[lentil-wellington]] Variant B / ground-lentil-pie experiments) and the modifications I want to try on top of Jamie's baseline in the next round of cooking.

=== STATUS — SCAFFOLD FOR ADVANCEMENT ===

Jamie's recipe is where I'm resetting the baseline. My previous iterations (see EXPERIMENTAL PROGRESS below) were built on top of Nisha Vora's lentil wellington filling — a fundamentally different starting point (mushroom-walnut-miso paste, no root vegetables, contemporary-vegan register). That direction plateaued at 'has potential' — solid but not advancing theory.

Jamie's recipe advances theory in a few small ways worth naming:
- ROOT-VEGETABLE-FORWARD base (swede + celeriac + leeks + carrots) instead of the mirepoix sofrito or the mushroom-walnut base
- CUMIN SEEDS as an unexpected aromatic — smoky-earthy dimension outside the rosemary/thyme/bay trinity
- DRIED PORCINI + MARMITE as the umami paste (blended smooth with onion + tomato paste)
- CRISPY ROSEMARY as garnish rather than melted-into-filling — the rosemary reads as a fresh top note rather than a woodsy background

Use this as the starting point to run the experiments below on. Won't be 'excellent' straight out of the box for what I'm after — needs the modifications.

=== EXPERIMENTAL DIRECTIONS TO TRY (BUILT ON JAMIE'S SCAFFOLD) ===

Things to try on top of Jamie's baseline in future cooks:

1. NUTMEG IN THE FILLING (not just the mash). Traditional cottage pies add nutmeg to the mash only. Adding ~1/4 tsp nutmeg to the FILLING is unusual — should extend the northern-european cream+mushroom+dairy tradition into the savory base itself. See [[dauphinois]] for the nutmeg + cream + roots pattern.

2. DRIED CRANBERRIES (SWEET-SAVORY POP). ~2 tbsp roughly chopped, mixed directly into the filling (not soaked, stays as chunks). Scaffolding from PBS's Spiced Pork Pie with Cranberries — traditional british meat-pie tradition that vegetarian versions almost never carry over. Would give the pie a sweet-savory dimension the current version lacks.

3. BEEF BOUILLON (OR DARK VEGETABLE BOUILLON). Add 1 cube or 1 tbsp better-than-bouillon paste to push the register toward meat-pie. Sits well with the marmite; extends rather than replaces the umami paste.

4. HEAVY CREAM INTO THE FILLING. 3-4 tbsp stirred in at the end. Lesson from earlier ground-lentil-pie experiments — cream is a powerful body upgrade in a lentil-mushroom filling. Pureed lentils are a strong sponge, so it doesn't read creamy — just adds fat and satisfaction. Precedent: Home Cooking Collective's vegetarian lentil pot pie uses whole milk in the filling.

5. BROWN THE BUTTER for the mash (or add a knob of brown butter to the filling). Deeper nutty base; goes with the northern-european register.

6. TOASTED WALNUTS. Same rule as [[lentil-wellington]]: toasted only, no almonds, no raw. Would add roasty meat-analog texture. Not standard in british cottage pies — original territory.

7. CUMIN + JUNIPER STACK. Jamie's cumin seeds is a good aromatic; adding a few crushed juniper berries (4-6) would extend into the british-german game-braise register. Both work together — different notes.

8. TAMARIND + WORCESTERSHIRE. Add 1 tbsp each to the umami paste alongside the marmite. Anglican depth condiments already established as effective in the Variant B experiments.

=== HAZARD FROM PRIOR EXPERIMENTS ===

FRESH DILL + TOMATO PASTE + FRESH DICED ONIONS = HAMBURGER-Y register (diner meatloaf, not british cottage pie). This is a specific 3-way combination — not a hazard for Jamie's recipe as-written because he uses ROSEMARY (not dill). If you swap the herb slot to dried dill AND keep the tomato paste AND keep fresh diced onion, you land in hamburger territory. Jamie's rosemary + tomato + onion is a well-established combination and works fine.

The hazard is specifically about DILL with tomato + onion. If you're experimenting with dill as an herb here, drop either the tomato paste or the fresh onion first.

=== HEAVY CREAM LESSON FROM PRIOR EXPERIMENTS ===

3-4 tbsp heavy cream stirred into the filling AFTER the vegetables/lentils cook, when the filling would otherwise be moldable-dry. What this DOESN'T do: make the filling read creamy. What it DOES do: adds fat, keeps the filling from drying out during the bake, makes the whole pie read more satisfying per bite. Was the single biggest quality upgrade in the earlier ground-lentil-pie experiments. Should transfer to Jamie's baseline.

=== LEMON — DON'T FORGET IT (LESSON FROM PRIOR EXPERIMENTS) ===

Earlier ground-lentil-pie iterations included 1 tbsp lemon juice in the filling. Once I FORGOT it and the pie read noticeably flatter — the savory-heavy mushroom/walnut/miso base needed the bright note. Jamie's recipe doesn't include lemon; worth trying to add 1 tbsp lemon juice at the end to see if it lifts the pie the same way it did in the Nisha-derived version.

=== TOASTED WALNUTS ARE THE ONLY VALID NUT (IF ADDING NUTS) ===

Carrying over from [[lentil-wellington]]: if you add nuts to the filling, TOASTED WALNUTS only. Almonds MAKE IT WORSE (sweet-crunchy vs savory-earthy). Raw untoasted walnuts MAKE IT WORSE (take the umami slot without filling it). Not in Jamie's recipe but a legitimate addition to try.

=== TRIED AND REJECTED (FROM PRIOR ITERATIONS) ===

Things I tested in the earlier ground-lentil-pie experiments that didn't stick:

- PUREED CELERY WITH THE MUSHROOMS. Added depth initially but pushed the pie into STEW TERRITORY quickly. If you want that direction, [[lentil-mushroom-potato-stew]] does it better as an actual stew. Jamie uses celeriac (celery root) instead — related but different behavior; the dense root doesn't turn stew-y the way chopped celery does.
- DIJON MUSTARD + TARRAGON (FRENCH DIRECTION). Fine but didn't add much over dill + thyme. Both mustard and tarragon are legitimate french flavors but they don't earn their place in this filling.

=== EXPERIMENTAL PROGRESS (HISTORICAL — BEFORE THE JAMIE SCAFFOLD RESET) ===

For context, here's the arc that led to this rewrite/reset:

1. Started with Nisha Vora's [[lentil-wellington]] filling as a base.
2. First anglican departure: butter + worcestershire/tamarind + dried dill. Distinctly more british.
3. Discovered the hamburger-y hazard: fresh dill + tomato paste + fresh onion.
4. Resolved by dropping all three fresh/tomato ingredients together as a unit.
5. Added crushed garlic late for bite.
6. Tried pureed celery — rejected (stew territory).
7. HEAVY CREAM discovered as the biggest upgrade.
8. Tried french direction (mustard + tarragon) — rejected (didn't add much).
9. Restructured as pot pie (skipping wellington's log-and-braid production).
10. Realized the whole line was 'has potential' but not advancing theory.
11. Web-scaffolded search found Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie as a more theory-advancing baseline (root veg + porcini + marmite + cumin seeds + crispy rosemary). RESET to Jamie's scaffold; folded prior lessons into the EXPERIMENTAL DIRECTIONS list above.

=== CROSS-REFERENCES ===

- [[lentil-wellington]]: Nisha Vora's original — a fundamentally different starting point (mushroom-walnut-miso paste, no root vegetables, wellington log-in-braided-pastry format). Where the earlier iterations of this pie started.
- [[turnip-yam-pie]]: the other pot-pie in the cookbook (turnips + sweet potatoes + swiss chard + bouillon gravy under a single crust). Different filling entirely but useful for pot-pie format decisions (crust vs panko vs mashed potato topping).
- [[dauphinois]]: the cream + nutmeg + roots pattern in a gratin format. Reference for the nutmeg-in-filling experiment.
- [[lentil-mushroom-potato-stew]]: the french stew form of a lentil + mushroom + celery dish. If the pie starts reading stew-y, this is where that flavor actually belongs.

=== SOURCES ===

- Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie: https://thehappyfoodie.co.uk/recipes/jamie-olivers-allotment-cottage-pie-with-root-veg-porcini-mushrooms-marmite-and-crispy-rosemary/
- Scaffolding cranberry proportion: PBS Spiced Pork Pie with Cranberries (https://www.pbs.org/food/recipes/spiced-pork-pie-cranberries)
- Dairy-in-filling precedent: Home Cooking Collective Vegetarian Lentil Pot Pie with Mushrooms & Leeks (https://homecookingcollective.com/lentil-vegetable-pot-pie-mushrooms-leeks/)
